questions.prompt: Use the horizontal line test on the graph of f(x) = x³ - x. Does f have an inverse function?
questions.prompt_markup: Use the horizontal line test on the graph of f(x) = x³ - x. Does f have an inverse function?

choices.text: No: the horizontal line y = 0 meets the graph three times (x = -1, 0, 1), so f is not one-to-one.
Yes: f is a polynomial, and every polynomial passes the horizontal line test, so f has an inverse function.
Yes: every cubic passes the horizontal line test, because its graph rises from left to right, so f is one-to-one.
No: the vertical line x = 0 meets the graph three times, so f fails the vertical line test and is not one-to-one.

questions.correct_answer: No: the horizontal line y = 0 meets the graph three times (x = -1, 0, 1), so f is not one-to-one.
questions.grading_note: One horizontal line meeting the graph more than once is enough. The others overgeneralize or confuse the tests (f is a function, so it passes the vertical line test).

questions.prompt: Why is g(x) = x² - 4, without a domain restriction, not the inverse of f(x) = √(x + 4)?
questions.prompt_markup: Why is g(x) = x² - 4, without a domain restriction, not the inverse of f(x) = √(x + 4)?

choices.text: Because f(g(2)) ≠ 2, so the composition fails even for positive inputs.
f(g(x)) = √(x²) = |x|, which is not x when x < 0; g is the inverse only on x ≥ 0 (the range of f).
Because g(x) = x² - 4 is not a function, since it gives two outputs for each input.
Because g(f(x)) = (√(x + 4))² - 4 is undefined for every x, so the composition test cannot be done.

questions.correct_answer: f(g(x)) = √(x²) = |x|, which is not x when x < 0; g is the inverse only on x ≥ 0 (the range of f).
questions.grading_note: √(x²) = |x|. The others are false: g(f(x)) = x for x ≥ -4, g is a function, and f(g(2)) = 2.
